questions.q: Which statement best describes intracellular potassium?
Match the key concept in Na/K ATPase with its correct interpretation.
opts: Moves potassium out of cells only
questions.exp: Na/K ATPase maintains intracellular potassium. (Book p968)

questions.q: A patient is being evaluated for insulin effect. Which finding or action is most appropriate?
questions.exp: Insulin promotes cellular potassium uptake. (Book p968)

questions.q: In the context of daily intake, the principal ___ is:
questions.exp: The regulation diagram shows daily intake around 100 mEq. (Book p968)

questions.q: Which option is the odd one out regarding proximal tubule?
questions.exp: Most filtered potassium is reabsorbed in the PCT. (Book p969)

questions.q: Assess these statements about thick ascending limb: I the first statement is correct; II the second statement is incorrect.
questions.exp: The TAL reabsorbs potassium with NKCC2. (Book p969)

questions.q: What is the characteristic value or relationship for collecting duct?
opts: Variable distal secretion regulated by aldosterone
questions.exp: Final potassium excretion is regulated distally. (Book p969)

questions.q: A clinical decision depends on aldosterone. Which choice is best?
questions.exp: Aldosterone promotes sodium uptake and potassium secretion. (Book p969)

questions.q: Which statement best describes significant potassium level?
questions.exp: The chapter labels potassium below 2–2.5 as significant. (Book p970)

questions.q: Match the key concept in ECG pattern with its correct interpretation.
opts: Flattened T waves with prominent U waves
questions.exp: Hypokalemia produces T-wave flattening, U waves and QT/QU changes. (Book p971)

questions.q: A patient is being evaluated for urine potassium/creatinine. Which finding or action is most appropriate?
opts: Any value rules out renal loss
questions.exp: The urine potassium/creatinine ratio helps identify renal wasting. (Book p972)

questions.q: In the context of low urine potassium, the principal ___ is:
opts: Conservation from extrarenal loss or cellular shift
questions.exp: Low urinary potassium means the kidney is conserving potassium. (Book p972)

questions.q: Which option is the odd one out regarding dangerous ECG treatment?
questions.exp: Calcium is the immediate membrane-stabilizing therapy. (Book p973)

questions.q: Assess these statements about insulin-glucose: I the first statement is correct; II the second statement is incorrect.
questions.exp: Insulin shifts potassium intracellularly; glucose prevents hypoglycemia. (Book p974)

questions.q: What is the characteristic value or relationship for dialysis?
opts: Only changes ECG without removing K
questions.exp: Dialysis is a definitive removal strategy when indicated. (Book p975)

questions.q: A clinical decision depends on digoxin toxicity. Which choice is best?
opts: Can produce hyperkalemia through Na/K ATPase inhibition
questions.exp: Digoxin inhibits Na/K ATPase and may raise serum potassium. (Book p975)
